= CHERIoT memory subsystem: checker 1 (tag path) microarchitecture
:toc: left
:toclevels: 2
:sectnums:
:imagesdir: figures
:fpv: ../opentitan/hw/ip/cheriot_mem_sys/fpv

FPV checker 1 of `cheriot_mem_sys` checks the tag path, from the core port `cored_tl_d` to the
RMW (read-modify-write) filter's downstream port. This doc shows how each check of the
checker 1 testplan, and checker 1's part of the subsystem testplan, is
done in the testbench; the testplan gives what each check proves. The contracts and proof
order are in the xref:cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc#tag_path[TB architecture], how the
design works in the xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc[design architecture],
and the TL-UL rules in the xref:../../tlul_abvip/tb_arch/tlul_abvip_uarch.adoc[TL-UL ABVIP].

== Overview

=== Boundary

*Rule:* checker 1 holds the real tag path: the core's tag filter with its WTRC
(write-to-read-and-compare filter), the 2:1 tag arbiter, the tag clear squash and the RMW filter.
The testbench plays every block around it.

* *Plays the host:* the ABVIP assumes the host's TL-UL rules and asserts the device's. *Plays the
  device:* the reverse. *Checks both ends* (`CheckBoth`): assumes nothing, asserts every rule.
* 21 testpoints in five groups: tag filter (6), WTRC (3), 2:1 tag arbiter (3), RMW filter (5),
  and alerts, contracts, protocol and environment (4). The composition testpoints
  `tag_read_after_write` and `tag_no_deadlock` have no property here: they follow from the checks
  of checkers 1 to 3.

'''

=== Testbench structure

*Rule:* one FPV environment serves the whole subsystem ([TB] One environment, one task per
checker). The FPV top `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_env` holds `cheriot_mem_sys` with every input free.
The shared checker, bound into the design, holds `tpchk_checker`: checker 1's checks and its
rules on the neighbours. Each rule is written with `ENV_RULE`: an assumption in formal, an
assertion in simulation. Only the bind and the FPV top's port list name RTL nets.

[[environment]]
== Environment

*Rule:* every rule on what checker 1's neighbours send sits in the `rules:` section of
link:{fpv}/tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv[`tpchk_checker.sv`]: a TL-UL ABVIP on each played port,
holding TL-UL's own rules only, and this design's restrictions on top, each naming its assumption
([DR] Assumptions) or contract ([TB] Contracts).

=== Tasks

[cols="2,5,4",options="header"]
|===
|Task |Checks |Rules beyond the common set

|`task_TagPath_Main` |every safety check, the alert checks (they need no fairness), every cover
|-
|`task_TagPath_TagsRspTaken` |the RMW filter takes every downstream answer (contract C4, `contracts` _RMW filter takes answers_, CHK_CONTRACTS_05) |the engine's tag filter takes each meta answer at
once (contract C3b)
|`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered` |`tf_flow` _request eventually accepted_ (CHK_TF_FLOW_03) and _request
eventually answered_ (CHK_TF_FLOW_04); `arb_flow` _no starvation_ (CHK_ARB_FLOW_03); `rmw_single_op`
_every operation answered_ (CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_04); `contracts` _RMW request accepted and answered_
(CHK_CONTRACTS_02, contract C2). Runs once checker 2 has proven contract C1 ([TB] Proof order,
stage 4) |contract C3b; the tag access checker accepts and answers (contract C1); `xbar_main`
accepts and answers (assumption A10); the core takes every answer (premise P5)
|===

* *Why three tasks:* contract C3b in the main task would void every check on an engine answer
  that waits. The two liveness tasks cannot merge: checker 2 proves contract C1 assuming contract
  C4, so C4 is proven without C1.
* A core that breaks its access order is out of scope ([TP] Not covered by this testplan), so
  every task keeps assumptions A3 and A4.

'''

=== Tag filter

*Rule:* each request on `cored_tl_d` is checked against the tag filter model at `cored_tl_h` and
the meta port; each answer on `cored_tl_d` against its joined parts ([TP] Tag filter).

[[tf_model]]
==== Tag filter model

*Rule:* the model keeps every core request in order, from its first cycle on `cored_tl_d` until
its answer is taken, joins its xbar answer and meta answer as they arrive, and predicts what the
tag filter must send ([ToO] Tag Filter, WTRC). It drives no port. The core is played by
`u_abvip_core` and the rules.

===== What the model watches and predicts

[[tf_model_memory]]
===== What the model remembers

*Rule:* the model keeps one record per core request, from the cycle the core presents it until
the core takes its answer. At most two are open, a third only in the cycle an answer frees a place
(assumption A2). Every request gets a record, because the tag returned with W1 and the WTRC's tag
write depend on the requests before it.

[cols="4,4",options="header"]
|===
|For each request, the model remembers |Which checks use it

|what it is: a read, W0 or W1 of a capability load, a write, or a word of a capability store to
the NVM; its address, `a_source`, data, and whether it needs a lookup |what must appear on
`cored_tl_h` and the meta port (`tf_forward`, `tf_lookup`, `wtrc_store`)
|whether it has been accepted, forwarded to `xbar_main`, and looked up |nothing is sent twice or
invented (`tf_forward`, `tf_lookup`)
|its answer from `xbar_main`, once back, with its error flag |the answer's fields and `d_error`
(`tf_forward`, `tf_errors`)
|its meta answer, once back, with its tag and error flag |the answer's tag and `d_error`
(`tf_sticky_tag`, `tf_errors`)
|for a word of a capability store to the NVM: whether it matched, and whether its tag write is
owed |the WTRC checks (`wtrc_compare`, `wtrc_faults`)
|===

*Which answer belongs to which request.* `xbar_main` answers in request order (assumption A7)
and the meta path returns one answer at a time, so each answer that comes back belongs to the
oldest request still waiting for that kind of answer. The answer due to the core is always the
oldest open request's. A part that arrives in a cycle counts in that cycle: the tag filter may
pass it straight through.

*The tag returned with W1.* The tag of W0's answer is kept, even when that answer has an error,
given back with the answer to the W1 that follows, then forgotten: the W1 answer's tag must be the
kept tag, or 0 when nothing is kept. A write answered between W0 and W1 leaves the kept tag alone. A
plain read answered between them is a case the spec leaves open, so that W1's tag is not checked. An
owed WTRC tag write is kept apart from the records, because it may leave the meta port a cycle after
its request's record closes.

.Example: a capability load of `0x1000_1238`, whose stored tag is 1
[cols="1,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Step |What happens |What the model expects

|1 |The core presents W0, a hinted `Get` of `0x1000_1238`. The model opens record 1: W0 of a
capability load, needs a lookup |the same `Get` on `cored_tl_h`, and a lookup of tag word
`0x1100_8C48`, bit 7, on the meta port, both in this cycle
|2 |The core presents W1, `0x1000_123C`. Record 2: W1, no lookup |the `Get` on `cored_tl_h`; no
lookup
|3 |`xbar_main` answers. Record 1 is the oldest waiting for that answer, so it is W0's |no answer
to the core yet: W0's meta answer is still out
|4 |The meta answer comes back with tag 1. It is W0's. Both parts of W0 are in |W0's answer to the
core in this cycle, with `xbar_main`{empty}'s data and tag 1. The model keeps tag 1
|5 |`xbar_main` answers W1. Record 2 has no lookup, so it is complete |W1's answer to the core in
this cycle, with tag 1, the kept tag. The model forgets it
|===

==== Tracker

*Rule:* the tracker follows one core request, chosen in its first cycle by `pick` (an input the
tool may set to anything, so every request gets followed in some trace). It keeps that request's
xbar answer if the tag filter takes it early (66 bits) and gives it back when the request's answer
is due. `tf_forward` _answer has host fields_ and `tf_errors` _merged error keeps integrity_ use
it; keeping every request's xbar answer would cost about 130 flops.

* No cover of its own: the covers of those two checks show it working.
* In simulation `pick` is 1: the tracker follows the next request whenever it is free.

'''

[[uw_tf_forward]]
==== tf_forward: every access forwarded once

Testplan. The tag filter passes
each core request to `xbar_main` once, unchanged and in the same cycle, and answers with the xbar
answer's fields as soon as the answer's last part is in.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_forwarded unchanged_ (CHK_TF_FORWARD_01) |a request is presented on
`cored_tl_d`, not yet forwarded, not a capability store to the NVM |the same request on `cored_tl_h`
in the same cycle, every A-channel field equal |Main
|_no extra host request_ (CHK_TF_FORWARD_02) |a request is presented
on `cored_tl_h` |a core request presented and not yet forwarded |Main
|_accepted after forwarded_ (CHK_TF_FORWARD_03) |a core request is
accepted |its xbar request is taken now, or was before |Main
|_answer has host fields_ (CHK_TF_FORWARD_04) |the tracked request's
answer is presented |its xbar answer has arrived; the answer's `d_opcode`, `d_size`, `d_source`,
`d_data`, data integrity equal it; the response integrity too, unless a meta error is merged |Main
|_answer on last part_ (CHK_TF_FORWARD_05) |the oldest open request's
last part has arrived; an answer is presented |the answer is presented then, and not before |Main
|===

'''

[[uw_tf_lookup]]
==== tf_lookup: when a tag is looked up

Testplan. A lookup goes out, in
the request's first cycle, exactly when the request needs one: W0 of a capability load or any
write, to a tagged region, in CHERIoT mode, except a capability store to the NVM.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_lookup in same cycle_ (CHK_TF_LOOKUP_01) |a request that needs a
lookup is presented, its lookup not yet taken, no tag write owed or possible |a meta request in the
same cycle |Main
|_no unneeded lookup_ (CHK_TF_LOOKUP_02) |a meta request is presented
that is not an owed or possible tag write |a presented request that needs a lookup whose lookup is
not yet taken |Main
|_lookup carries valid integrity_ (CHK_TF_LOOKUP_03) |a request is
presented on the meta port |a valid command integrity |Main
|===

'''

|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_tag word and bit_ (CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_01) |a lookup is
presented |the tag word of the core request's address as `a_address`, its tag bit as the bit
select |Main
|_write carries its tag_ (CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_02) |a write's
lookup is presented |its tag equals the core's tag sideband |Main
|_Get only for a read_ (CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_03) |a lookup is
presented |a `Get` exactly when the core request is one |Main
|===

'''

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_answer tag follows rule_ (CHK_TF_STICKY_TAG_01) |an answer is
presented, not to a capability store, and its tag is checked |the tag the model gives |Main

Testplan. The answer has

|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

[[uw_tf_flow]]
==== tf_flow: no stall, no lost answer

Testplan. The meta port always
takes its answers, so the two tag filters sharing the RMW filter cannot deadlock, and every
request is accepted and answered once.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_meta answer taken_ (CHK_TF_FLOW_01) |a meta answer is offered
|`d_ready` in the same cycle |Main
|_no extra answer_ (CHK_TF_FLOW_02) |an answer is presented on
`cored_tl_d` |an accepted, unanswered request |Main
|_request eventually accepted_ (CHK_TF_FLOW_03) |a request is presented
|it is accepted, at some point |EveryReqAnswered
|_request eventually answered_ (CHK_TF_FLOW_04) |an accepted request is
unanswered |the oldest one's answer is taken, at some point; answers come in order (contract C6), so
each one's is |EveryReqAnswered
|===

=== WTRC

*Rule:* a capability store to the NVM is checked at its `Get` on `cored_tl_h`, on the meta port
(no lookup; the tag write), at its answer, and at the WTRC fault to the alert, each against the
model's WTRC sequence and whether each word matched ([TP] WTRC).

.Flowchart: one capability store to the NVM (click to expand)
[%collapsible]
====
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch_figures.svg#fig5["one capability store to the NVM, step by step",align=center,width=893,height=2156]
====

==== WTRC sequence

Part of the tag filter model (<<tf_model>>).

*Rule:* the model follows the capability store sequence of [ToO] WTRC, to tell an in-sequence
request from an out-of-sequence one and to know when W1's tag write is owed. The ways marked "out
of scope" need a core that breaks its access order; the model keeps them so it stays defined for
every input.

[cols="2,3,5",options="header"]
|===
|Stage |Out of sequence here (a fault) |Moves on when

|no capability open |a W1 |a W0 is accepted: W0 taken
|W0 taken |anything but the W1 of the same capability |its W1 is accepted: W1 taken. Out of
scope: another W0 opens a new capability
|W1 taken |any request |the tag write is taken: tag write sent; or W1's answer is taken without a
tag write: no capability open. Out of scope: a W0 is accepted
|tag write sent |a W1, or a W0 |W1's answer is taken: no capability open. Out of scope: a W0 is
accepted
|===

* A request is judged in its first cycle. In the cycle W1's answer is taken, it is judged as if no
  capability were open: the next W0 may be taken then (assumption A4).
* Whether W0 matched is kept at W0's NVM answer. At W1's NVM answer, if both matched and no fault,
  the tag write is owed until the meta port takes it; otherwise W1 is answered with `d_error`.
* *Broken sequence* (out of scope): the open capability's tag write becomes a _possible_ tag
  write, neither required nor forbidden, and W1's `d_error` is not checked; the faulty request
  and the alert still are. The tag filter checks let a possible tag write through.

'''

[[fault_causes]]
==== Fault causes

Part of the tag filter model (<<tf_model>>); the alert checks read it.

*Rule:* the model flags each fault cause of [ToO] Error Handling in the cycle it occurs, and
remembers that one occurred since reset; the alert checks compare the WTRC's fault input with
these.

[cols="5,3",options="header"]
|===
|Cause |When the model sees it

|a capability store word out of sequence, partial, or with a bad command or data integrity |its
first cycle
|a bad response integrity on a capability store word's NVM answer |the NVM answer arrives
|any other request out of sequence |its first cycle
|===

The checks also use "a cause has occurred since reset".

'''

[[uw_wtrc_store]]
==== wtrc_store: a capability store to the NVM reads, never writes

Testplan. A capability store to
the NVM reaches `xbar_main` as a `Get` of its word, makes no lookup, and is answered `AccessAck`,
untagged, by the WTRC.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_sent as a full-word Get_ (CHK_WTRC_STORE_01) |a capability store
word is presented, not yet forwarded |a full-word `Get` of its word on `cored_tl_h` in the same
cycle |Main
|_Get has valid command integrity_ (CHK_WTRC_STORE_02) |that `Get` is
presented |a valid command integrity |Main
|_no lookup for a capability store_ (CHK_WTRC_STORE_03) |a capability
store word is presented |no meta request, or only an owed or possible tag write |Main
|_untagged AccessAck answer_ (CHK_WTRC_STORE_04) |a capability store
word's answer is presented |`AccessAck`, untagged, `d_source` its `a_source`, valid response
integrity |Main
|===

'''

[[uw_wtrc_compare]]
==== wtrc_compare: which stores set the tag

Testplan. Each word is
compared with what the NVM holds; only when both words match does W1 become the capability's tag
write, ahead of any lookup; a mismatch fails the store with `d_error`, never with an alert.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_W0 error on mismatch_ (CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_01) |W0's answer is
presented, no fault, its NVM answer in |`d_error` exactly when W0 did not match |Main
|_only the owed tag write_ (CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_02) |a meta request is
presented while a tag write is owed |it is the tag write: a write of tag 1 to the capability's tag
word and tag bit |Main
|_W1 answered after tag write_ (CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_03) |W1's answer is
presented and its tag write was owed |the tag write's answer has arrived; `d_error` is its error
|Main
|_W1 error on mismatch_ (CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_04) |W1's answer is
presented, no fault, no tag write owed or possible |`d_error` |Main
|_no alert without a cause_ (CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_05) |the WTRC's fault
input is raised |a fault cause has occurred since reset |Main
|_answer after NVM answer_ (CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_06) |W0's or W1's
answer is presented |its NVM answer has arrived, now or before |Main
|===

'''

[[uw_wtrc_faults]]
==== wtrc_faults: what the core cannot produce

Testplan. A capability store
word with a bad integrity fails with `d_error`, sets no tag and raises the fatal alert. Faults
from a word out of sequence or partial need a core that breaks its access order, which is out of
scope, so only the integrity faults are reached.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_faulty word answered with error_ (CHK_WTRC_FAULTS_01) |a faulty
word's answer is presented, its NVM answer in |`d_error`; no tag write is owed for it, so
`tf_lookup` _no unneeded lookup_ fails on one |Main
|_faulty word raises alert_ (CHK_WTRC_FAULTS_02) |a faulty capability
store word is seen |the alert request rises, at some point |Main
|===

* The cover of case _bad NVM response integrity_ is unreachable while the temporary integrity
  rule holds.
* The debug cover `dbg_cover_NvmCapStore_BadCmdIntg_TagWritten_NoDErrorToCore` shows a finding
  ([FD]): a store word with a bad command integrity answered without `d_error`, its tag written; it
  becomes unreachable once R16 is fixed. It is no testplan case, so it is not in the check map.

'''

=== 2:1 tag arbiter

*Rule:* a request leaving the arbiter must be one input's request, unchanged but for `a_source`,
which is shifted left by one with the input number in bit 0 (the forwarded request). An answer from
the RMW filter must reach the input named in bit 0 of its `d_source`, with `d_source` shifted right
by one. Both happen in the same cycle ([TP] 2:1 tag arbiter). A check about one input runs on each
input in a loop, so a simulation checks both.

[%collapsible]

====

each request it accepts to the RMW filter once, with its input number added at the bottom of

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_keeps its own sideband_ (CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01) |a request is accepted
on input `i` |the output takes its forwarded request in that cycle, with its own bit select and tag
|Main
|_from the named input_ (CHK_ARB_FORWARD_02) |a request is presented
at the output |it is the forwarded request of the input named in bit 0 of its `a_source`, taken with
it |Main
|_core request unchanged_ (CHK_ARB_FORWARD_03) |the output presents a
request from input 0 |the RMW filter's upstream request equals it |Main
|===

'''

[[uw_arb_return]]
==== arb_return: each answer to the input that asked

Testplan. Each answer goes back
only to the input that asked, with the input number taken off `a_source` and nothing else
changed.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_answer to its input_ (CHK_ARB_RETURN_01) |an answer is presented at
input `i` |the RMW filter presents an answer naming `i` |Main
|_taken with its input_ (CHK_ARB_RETURN_02) |as _source shifted back_
|the RMW filter's answer is taken exactly when its input takes it |Main
|_source shifted back_ (CHK_ARB_RETURN_03) |the RMW filter presents an
answer |the input named in bit 0 of its `d_source` gets `d_source` shifted right by one |Main
|_fields unchanged_ (CHK_ARB_RETURN_04) |as _source shifted back_
|every other D-channel field and the tag unchanged; `d_data` only in an `AccessAckData` |Main

[[uw_arb_flow]]
==== arb_flow: no added cycle, no starvation

Testplan. The arbiter adds no
cycle in either direction and never leaves one input waiting for ever.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_alone in same cycle_ (CHK_ARB_FLOW_01) |input `i` presents and the
other does not |the output presents its forwarded request in that cycle |Main
|_answer at once_ (CHK_ARB_FLOW_02) |the RMW filter presents an answer
|the input named in bit 0 of its `d_source` presents it in that cycle |Main
|_no starvation_ (CHK_ARB_FLOW_03) |input `i` presents a request |it is
accepted, at some point, while the RMW filter keeps accepting (contract C2, proven here)
|EveryReqAnswered
|===

The arbitration policy is an open question to the designers.

'''

=== RMW filter

*Rule:* each downstream request must be the `Get` or the write-back the RMW model expects next,
with the fields the spec gives; each upstream answer must carry the tag bit read, an `AccessAck`,
or the write-back's answer ([TP] RMW filter). After a faulty `Get` answer nothing about that
write is checked (<<rmw_model,RMW model>>).

.Flowcharts: one RMW tag read, then one RMW tag write (click to expand)
[%collapsible]
====
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch_figures.svg#fig7["one RMW tag read, step by step",align=center,width=890,height=1459]

image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch_figures.svg#fig8["one RMW tag write, step by step",align=center,width=890,height=1450]
====

[[rmw_model]]
==== RMW model

*Rule:* the model follows the RMW filter's one operation, from its acceptance upstream to its
answer taken, and says which downstream request may come next and what the answer must be ([ToO]
RMW Filter). It drives no port; `u_abvip_tags` plays the tag access checker.

===== What the model watches and predicts

.The RMW model: what it watches, what it keeps, and which check compares each prediction
image::cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_tag_path_uarch_figures.svg#fig9["RMW model: what it watches, keeps and predicts",align=center,width=900,height=711]

[cols="1,4,3,8,4",options="header"]
|===
|Point |Watches |Sent by |The model keeps or predicts |Checked by

|(1) |a request upstream, after the tag clear squash |RTL arbiter, from either tag filter |the
operation: read or write, meta word, bit select `b`, tag `t`, `a_source` |input here; the arbiter
checks
|(2) |the downstream answer |`u_abvip_tags` |the `Get` answer's word `W`, its `d_error`, whether
its integrity is broken; then the write-back's answer |input
|(3) |the downstream request |RTL RMW filter |the operation's `Get` of its meta word with its
`a_source`; for a write whose bit differs and whose `Get` had no error, one full-word `PutFullData`
of `W` with bit `b` set to `t`; nothing else |<<uw_rmw_read,`rmw_read`>>,
<<uw_rmw_write_skip,`rmw_write_skip`>>, <<uw_rmw_write_back,`rmw_write_back`>>,
<<uw_rmw_single_op,`rmw_single_op`>>, <<uw_rmw_errors,`rmw_errors`>>
|(4) |`a_ready` and the answer upstream |RTL RMW filter |accept only with no operation unanswered,
or as the only one, a read, is answered; answer bit `b` of `W` for a read, `AccessAck` for an equal
bit, else the write-back's answer; `d_error` exactly from the meta SRAM; one answer per operation
|<<uw_rmw_read,`rmw_read`>>, <<uw_rmw_write_skip,`rmw_write_skip`>>,
<<uw_rmw_write_back,`rmw_write_back`>>, <<uw_rmw_single_op,`rmw_single_op`>>,
<<uw_rmw_errors,`rmw_errors`>>
|(5) |the device and integrity faults to the alert logic |RTL RMW filter |a fault only after a meta
SRAM answer with `d_error`, or a bad response or data integrity, since reset
|<<uw_contracts,`contracts`>>
|===

* *Faulty `Get` answer* (no `d_error`, a broken response or data integrity): the alert is
  raised, and nothing the filter sends or answers for that write is checked.
* The arbiter takes an answer with the `d_ready` of the input it returns to: the tag filter keeps
  it at 1 (`tf_flow`); contract C3b keeps the engine's at 1 in the liveness tasks.

'''

===== What the model remembers

*Rule:* the RMW filter works on one operation at a time, so the model keeps one: the request (read
or write, its meta word, bit select `b`, tag `t` and `a_source`), the word `W` its `Get` brought
back with that answer's error and integrity, and the write-back's answer. It also keeps how far
the operation has got, in the stages of the spec ([ToO] RMW Filter), and allows only the next
downstream request and the answer that stage permits.

[cols="3,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Stage (spec name) |Downstream request allowed |Upstream

|no operation |the `Get` of the request presented upstream, in the cycle it is accepted |a request
may be accepted
|`Passthrough` |its `Get`, once |nothing
|`Fill`, waiting |nothing |the answer may leave in the cycle `W` arrives
|`Fill`, `W` in |for a write whose bit `b` of `W` differs from `t`, with no error: the write-back,
`W` with bit `b` set to `t`; otherwise nothing |a read, an equal-bit write or a `Get` with an error
is answered; after a read the next request may come in, in the same cycle
|`WriteBackReq` |nothing |the answer may leave in the cycle the write-back's answer arrives
|`WriteBackAck` |nothing |the write-back's answer, with its `d_opcode` and `d_error`
|===

.Example: a write of tag 1 to bit 7 of meta word `0x1100_8C48`, which holds `0x0000_0000`
[cols="1,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Step |What happens |What the model expects

|1 |The write is accepted upstream |a full-word `Get` of `0x1100_8C48` downstream, with the
write's `a_source`, and nothing else
|2 |The `Get` comes back: `W` is `0x0000_0000`, no error. Bit 7 is 0, the tag is 1: they differ
|one write-back: a full-word `PutFullData` of `0x0000_0080` to `0x1100_8C48`; no answer upstream
yet
|3 |The write-back's answer comes back, no error |the write's answer upstream in this cycle:
`AccessAck`, no error; then the next request may be accepted
|===

Had bit 7 already been 1, step 2 would end the operation: no write-back, and an `AccessAck` answer
upstream. The tag access checker never answers in the cycle it takes a request (contract C10), so
the model needs no case for that.

[[uw_rmw_read]]
==== rmw_read: a read returns its bit

Testplan. A tag read reads its
whole meta word once and returns the one bit; a read right after a read is not held up.

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_Get of its meta word_ (CHK_RMW_READ_01) |a downstream request is
presented while the model expects a read's `Get` |a `Get` of the read's word with its `a_source`
|Main
|_returns its tag bit_ (CHK_RMW_READ_02) |a read's answer is presented
upstream |its `Get` answer has arrived; without `d_error`, the tag is bit `b` of `W` |Main
|_back-to-back read accepted_ (CHK_RMW_READ_03) |a read is presented as
the previous read is answered, downstream ready |it is accepted in that cycle |Main
|_Get carries valid integrity_ (CHK_RMW_READ_04) |any `Get` is presented
downstream, for a read or a write |a valid command integrity |Main
|===

'''

[[uw_rmw_write_skip]]

`4'hF`) of its word
|Main

presented |not while the current write's bit equals its tag |Main

answer is presented |`AccessAck` |Main

whose bit differs is answered upstream |its write-back's answer is presented downstream in that

`Get` or write-back is presented |the write's `a_source` |Main

Testplan. The RMW filter
works on one tag access at a time, answers each once, and sends the meta SRAM nothing it was not

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_one operation at a time_ (CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_01) |a request is

|_nothing else downstream_ (CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_02) |a downstream

|_every operation answered_ (CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_04) |an operation is

[[uw_rmw_errors]]

reports an error, nothing is written after it and the error reaches the requester; the filter

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]

|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

a meta SRAM answer with `d_error` |the alert request rises, at some point |Main

[[uw_contracts]]
==== contracts: what checker 1 proves for the other checkers

Testplan. Proven here, assumed in
checkers 2 and 3 ([TB] Contracts).

[cols="3,4,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Check |Looks when |Expects |Task

|_RMW request accepted and answered (contract C2)_ (CHK_CONTRACTS_02)
|a request is presented on the RMW filter's upstream port |it is accepted, at some point
|EveryReqAnswered
|_RMW filter takes answers (contract C4)_ (CHK_CONTRACTS_05) |an answer
is offered downstream |the RMW filter takes it, at some point |TagsRspTaken
|_core answers in order (contract C6)_ (CHK_CONTRACTS_07) |an answer is
presented on `cored_tl_d` |its `d_source` is the oldest unanswered request's `a_source` |Main
|_core meta request held (contract C7)_ (CHK_CONTRACTS_08) |a meta
request waits |it stays, with its tag and bit select, until taken |Main
|_tag path faults have causes (contract C8)_ (CHK_CONTRACTS_09) |a
fault input of the WTRC or the RMW filter is raised |one of its causes has occurred since reset
|Main
|===

* Contract C7 holds only if the core holds its requests (assumption A1, open an open question).
* Contract C8 is assumed nowhere: checker 3 cuts the RMW filter and the tag access checker, so it
  cannot see their causes. C8 serves the subsystem check `alert_causes` _alert only on a fault_
  (CHK_ALERT_CAUSES_01), with contract C9 from checker 3.

[[uw_tlul_protocol]]
==== tlul_protocol: every port follows TL-UL

Testplan. Check _TL-UL rules hold_ (CHK_TLUL_PROTOCOL_01): the TL-UL
rules on every port, assumed where the testbench drives and asserted where the design drives. No
property of its own: the six ABVIPs ([ABVIP] TL01 to TL13).

* Asserted, by port: the tag filter's answers on `cored_tl_d` and requests on `cored_tl_h`; the
  arbiter's answers on input 1; the RMW filter's requests downstream; both channels of arbiter
  input 0 and of the RMW filter upstream.
* Known design behaviour, recorded as a finding ([FD]): `u_abvip_m1` TL11 fails when the tag
  clear squash answers an engine `Put` with `AccessAckData`; `u_abvip_rmw` TL07 fails when the
  squash turns a `PutPartialData` with a gapped mask into a `Get`.

'''

[[uw_environment]]
==== environment: every rule can be met

Testplan. Covers only, one per rule: each shows that what the rule
allows still happens. A rule that makes its cover unreachable is too strict. The covers for the
rules of decision D23 are still to add (open decisions).

'''

=== State and bounds

*Rule:* every flop has the spec rule that needs it, and every bound the properties use has its
source.

The checker holds 773 flops of its own; the largest parts are the debug view's two logs (268 bits)
and the tag filter model's two records (200 bits). The ABVIPs hold 5,519 more, 5,401 of them in the
three lists left at the default size. No helper properties. The debug view is set in the
debug view uarch.

[cols="3,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Bound |Value |Source

|a request on `cored_tl_d` reaches `cored_tl_h` and the meta port |same cycle |`REQ_TF_16a`,
[ToO] Timing
|an answer's last part reaches `cored_tl_d` |same cycle |`REQ_TF_16b`
|the tag filter takes a meta answer |same cycle |`REQ_TF_14`
|an arbiter input reaches the output; an answer reaches its input |same cycle |`REQ_ARB_09`,
`REQ_ARB_10`
|a fault cause raises the alert request |no bound |the spec gives none (testplan premise P7)
|anything else |no bound |the checks follow the order of events, not cycle counts
|===

== Running it

[[jasper_setup]]
=== Files

*Rule:* checker 1's files sit in the opentitan checkout in `hw/ip/cheriot_mem_sys/fpv/tag_path/`;
the FPV top, the bind, the rule macro and the check script belong to the one FPV environment,
shared with the other checkers.

[cols="3,6",options="header"]
|===
|In `opentitan/hw/ip/cheriot_mem_sys/fpv/` |Holds

|`tag_path/tpchk_pkg.sv` |the testplan's definitions as types and functions
|`tag_path/tpchk_checker.sv` |port events, every check and cover (one banner section per testpoint), the two `CheckBoth` ABVIPs, and the rules: the four played-port ABVIPs and the rules
on top of them
|`tag_path/tpchk_tf_model.sv`, `tag_path/tpchk_rmw_model.sv` |the tag filter model with the
tracker; the RMW model
|`cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_env.sv`, `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_rule.svh` |shared: the FPV top; `ENV_RULE`,
an assumption under `FPV_ON`, an assertion otherwise
|`cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_checker.sv`, `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_checker_bind.sv` |shared: the one
checker, which holds `tpchk_checker`, and its bind, used in formal and simulation. Each bind sits
inside `default_nettype none`, so a misspelt net is an error
|`cheriot_mem_sys_fpv.core` |shared: the fusesoc core, every checker's files, the RTL and the
TL-UL ABVIP; target `formal`, top `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_env`
|===

=== Jasper setup

*Rule:* Jasper elaborates the whole design once; each checker 1 task takes its own checks, rules
and cut points.

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Setting |Meaning, default

|`TASKS` |tasks to make, names or globs; default every task of every checker
|`PROVE` |tasks to prove, names or globs; default none
|`FILES` |file list; default `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv.scr`
|`TIME_LIMIT`, `PER_PROP_LIMIT` |proof limits; default `1h`
|`FRESH` |`1`: ProofMaster and the prove cache off
|`PROPS` |only these properties, a fix's first check
|`FORMAL_JOBS`, `COV`, `WITH_PROVEN`, `ASSUME_ASSERTS` |shared, from `formal_ibex_cheriot/scripts`
|===

* *Load:* every file with `FPV_ON` and no run define; elaborate `cheriot_mem_sys_fpv_env` with
  Jasper's automatic covers generated; nothing blackboxed. One clock, `clk_i`; reset while
  `rst_ni` is low.
* *Tasks:* `tpchk_task` copies, per task, the checker's properties by label with their related
  covers, and the rules the task table gives it. No RTL assumption is copied: that leaves out
  `CoredReqHeld_M`, the four of `prim_alert_sender` and those of
  `prim_arbiter_ppc`, none of which limits a signal checker 1 reads. The arbiter's own liveness
  assertions, `NoStarvation_A` and `Fairness_A`, go only into `task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`
.
* *Cut points*, in each checker 1 task: the TBRE, the four access checkers, the 4:1 arbiter, the
  register file, and `u_dut.u_fpv_checker.u_tpchk_checker.pick`.
* *Cache:* ProofMaster in `proofmaster-<task>`. A reported result comes from a `FRESH` run
  whenever the rules or the checks changed since the last one.
* *Prove:* one run per task in `PROVE`; then the CEX, undetermined and unreachable lists,
  `results_<task>.txt` and `summary_<task>.txt`. Short limits first, to flush out testbench issues.
* *Hidden findings:* none in the script. To look past a known finding, add a session-only debug
  assumption `hide_<finding>` with ProofMaster off; it never appears in a reported result.

How to run it: one dvsim run per task (`fpv/README.md`, Run it with dvsim). The Jasper check
script is kept outside this repository.

=== Lint

* Verilator 5.048 (`--lint-only -Wall`), with and without `FPV_ON`, against the OpenTitan
  packages and the ABVIP's files; the FPV top elaborates with both binds on the RTL
  (`tools/verify.sh`).
* By design: `UNUSEDSIGNAL` on unused fields of whole port structs, and on signals read only by
  liveness properties (declared in lint pairs).
* Liveness properties sit inside `ifdef FPV_ON` and `ifndef VERILATOR`: Verilator rejects
  `s_eventually` and `strong(...)`.
* Covers whose sequence negates a signal compare it with `1'b0`: Verilator rejects `!` there.
